format.meaning: The requests the Companion sends to the server and the answers it gets, under `/companion/v1`. Each case's `input.request` is one request (its method, its path, its JSON body and, where it needs the account, its `headers`) and `expected` the answer (its HTTP status and its JSON body). `input.given` names what happened before the request, from the list under `given`. The server answers every case as written here; the Companion builds each request and reads each answer from its copy.
format.address: The server's address is the production deployment's `convex.site` URL. Every path under `/companion/v1` keeps answering as written here for as long as a Companion that uses it is installed anywhere: a change that old Companions couldn't read gets a new path.
format.requests: A request with a body is a POST with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every answer is JSON. A body the server can't read as the case shows (not JSON, a field missing or of the wrong type, a name or version that is empty or too long) is answered with status 400 and `{ "error": "invalid_request" }`. A Companion ignores fields it doesn't know in an answer.
linking: The Companion asks for a link with `POST /companion/v1/link`: `name` is what the player will see the computer called on the website (1 to 64 characters once trimmed), `version` the Companion's own version (1 to 32 characters).

The answer gives `code` to show the player, `secret` to poll with, `url` (the website's link page with the code in it, which the Companion opens in the browser), `expiresIn` (how many seconds the code lasts: 600) and `interval` (how many seconds to wait between polls).

The Companion then polls with `POST /companion/v1/link/poll` and its `secret`. `status` is `pending` until the signed-in player confirms the code on the link page. The first poll after that answers `linked` with `token`, the device token, and no later poll gives it again.

`expired` means this link is over, whatever the reason: the code ran out before anyone confirmed it, a confirmed code's token wasn't collected in time, the token was already given, or the server never gave that secret. The Companion stops polling and asks for a new link when the player wants one.

A code can be confirmed for `expiresIn` seconds and no longer. The token of a code confirmed in that time is given to a poll that arrives up to 30 seconds after the code ran out, so a code confirmed in its last seconds still links, and to no later poll. The Companion keeps polling at `interval` until it is answered `linked` or `expired`: it never has to count the time itself.

The Companion keeps the device token in its own config file, outside the game folder and readable by the player's user only, and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request that needs the account. It lasts until the player unlinks the computer on the website.
upload: The Companion uploads with `POST /companion/v1/upload` and its device token. `version` is the Companion's own version (1 to 32 characters). `recording` is `PriceWatchDB.recording` as the addon saved it, written as JSON the way `saved-variables.json` writes a parsed value: each format version's records under their own key, and under `v1` the `sessions` and `routes` by Session ID and the `ledger` and `characters` by character, every value the string the addon wrote, unchanged (`recording-v1.json`). A route goes with its Session.

The Companion may leave out a Session or a Ledger row it has already sent unchanged, and whatever else the recording holds (`count`, `current`, `mails`): the server reads none of it. It sends nothing from outside the recording.

`uploadedUpTo` in the answer is the latest record time in what the upload held, in the game's server time and never the server's clock: the time of the last row of the Session that goes on longest, or of a later Ledger row. The Companion writes it, with `linked = true`, into its data addon (`recording-v1.json`, `format.companion`), and the addon prunes up to it at the next login.

`uploadedUpTo` is null when the server read no record time: the upload held no rows, or the server couldn't read all of it (a format version it doesn't know yet, a Session without its `start` row), which it has stored all the same. The Companion then leaves the `uploadedUpTo` it wrote before as it is.

Sending a Session again is safe: the server keeps it once. A Session uploaded at a /reload and sent again longer, its `end` row turned into a `reload` row with more rows after it, takes the earlier copy's place.

Status 401 with `{ "error": "invalid_token" }` means the token is of no linked computer: the player unlinked it, or the server never gave it. The Companion stops uploading and shows that it isn't linked.

Status 413 with `{ "error": "too_large" }` means the request's body is over 8 MiB (8388608 bytes). Nothing of it was stored. An upload can be split over several requests, each with some of the Sessions.

Status 429 with `{ "error": "too_many_uploads" }` means this computer has already sent 30 uploads in the last hour. Every upload counts, whatever its answer, except one answered 429. `retryAfter`, also sent as the `Retry-After` header, is how many seconds to wait before the next one.

varies.meaning: The server makes these values up, so they differ on every run. A case shows an example. A runner checks the real value against the pattern, and puts the real `code`, `secret` and `token` where a later request or answer of the same link shows the example.

given.asked: The Companion asked for a link, as in the first case, and nobody has confirmed its code.
given.confirmed: As `asked`, and a signed-in player then confirmed the code on the link page.
given.collected: As `confirmed`, and one poll has already been answered with the device token.
given.ran out: As `asked`, and more than 600 seconds passed with nobody confirming the code.
given.uploaded: As `collected`, and the computer then sent the request of the case "a first upload is stored, and the answer says up to when" and was answered.
given.unlinked: As `collected`, and the player then unlinked the computer on the website.
given.30 uploads: As `collected`, and the computer then sent 30 uploads, the last of them just now.
